clue.text: Letter causes a bit of irritation

parts.note: an itch is a small irritation of the skin

explanation.surface: A single letter manages to be a minor annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes' is a link word. The answer is how the letter H is spelt out in full.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the written name of the eighth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Touch Roman wood, say?

parts.note: the phrase asks for the Latin way of warding off ill luck, as a Roman might say it

explanation.surface: A Roman superstitiously touching wood.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR garbled the clue; the page reads 'Touch Roman wood, say?'. Absit omen is Latin for 'may it not be an omen', said as English speakers say 'touch wood'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Latin phrase meaning may this not prove an omen, used to avert bad luck.

clue.text: Some say "What a boon, prohibition!"

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their letters is taken

explanation.surface: People exclaiming how welcome a ban is.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR garbled the clue; the page reads 'Some say "What a boon, prohibition!"'. 'say' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A ban on something by social custom or rule is a forbidding.

clue.text: Monster breaking Dulcie's heart — what a ram!

parts.note: the Hydra is the many-headed monster of Greek myth

indicators.note: breaking means the letters are broken up and reassembled
the heart of a word is its letters without the first and last

explanation.surface: A monster breaks poor Dulcie's heart and someone exclaims at a battering ram.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' strips the first and last letters from Dulcie, and 'breaking' rearranges what is left. 'ram' looks like a sheep but is the water pump.
explanation.definitionFit: A hydraulic ram is a pump driven by flowing water, so this is the kind of ram meant.

clue.text: Scurrilous Greek causes havoc in his street

indicators.note: causing havoc throws things into disorder, so the letters of the words that follow are jumbled

explanation.surface: A foul-mouthed Greek runs riot in the road where he lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'causes havoc' is the anagram signal and 'in' a link: rearrange HISSTREET.
explanation.definitionFit: In Homer's Iliad he is the ugly, abusive common soldier who rails at the Greek leaders.

clue.text: Middle Earth myth-maker — not like his metamorphosis

indicators.note: a metamorphosis is a complete change of form, so the letters change shape

explanation.surface: The creator of Middle Earth, transformed into someone unlike himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'his' is a link; 'metamorphosis' rearranges NOT LIKE. The OCR ran myth-maker and not together.
explanation.definitionFit: J. R. R. Tolkien invented the world of The Hobbit and The Lord of the Rings.

clue.text: Amounts are raised by a beloved Dutchman

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the letters are read upwards, so from the bottom

parts.note: sums are amounts of money

explanation.surface: Money is collected by a much-loved man from Holland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns SUMS ARE as one run, giving ERA SMUS. Erasmus took the name Desiderius, Latin for desired or beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderius Erasmus was the Dutch humanist scholar whose adopted first name means desired.

clue.text: Language of abuse

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to ... someone is to attack them with insults

explanation.surface: Words used to insult people.
explanation.definitionFit: Casual vocabulary outside standard speech, and a British verb meaning to berate someone with insults.

clue.text: Saucy ? Like hell !

definitions.meaning: read as like tartare sauce, the creamy mayonnaise dressing
Tartarus is the deepest pit of the Greek underworld

explanation.surface: Someone is called cheeky and indignantly denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' looks like cheeky, but here it means resembling tartare sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertaining to the Greek underworld of torment, and punningly to tartare sauce.

clue.text: Yugoslav dichotomy

definitions.meaning: a port city on the Dalmatian coast, then in Yugoslavia, now Croatia

explanation.surface: A division in the former Yugoslavia.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dalmatian city of the former Yugoslavia, and a division into two.

clue.text: Seeds of an evil evil in South Africa

parts.note: evil can mean bad
evil can also mean ill, as in ill will
an is the indefinite article, giving A

explanation.surface: A sinister crop of seeds grows on South African soil.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped the second 'evil'; the page prints it twice. 'in' is a link, and A from 'an' goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabadilla is a Mexican plant of the lily family whose seeds yield an insecticide.

clue.text: Than longen folk to goon on pilgrimages

definitions.text: Than longen folk to goon on pilgrimages

parts.words: Than longen folk to goon on pilgrimages
parts.note: a line from the opening of Chaucer's Canterbury Tales prologue, which names the spring month when people long to go on pilgrimage

explanation.surface: A line of Middle English verse about people longing to set off on pilgrimage.
explanation.walkthrough: Chaucer's prologue opens 'Whan that Aprill with his shoures soote' and goes on 'Thanne longen folk to goon on pilgrimages': the month is the season the line describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The springtime month Chaucer names as the time folk long to travel to Canterbury.

clue.text: A girl in spite of being a gunner

parts.note: tho is the informal short spelling of though, meaning in spite of that
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A girl carries on despite serving in the artillery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. RA (Royal Artillery) is a standard crossword way of saying gunner.
explanation.definitionFit: Thora is a female first name, as in the actress Thora Hird.

clue.text: Alien settler admits he is 1,000 years old

parts.note: the man speaking would say I'm M, M being the Roman numeral for a thousand
to admit something is to say I grant it

explanation.surface: A newcomer from abroad confesses to being a thousand years old.
explanation.walkthrough: The man speaks for himself: 'I'm M, I grant' is him admitting he is a thousand. The OCR added a colon and a space in 1,000.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who comes from abroad to live permanently in a country is a foreign settler.

clue.text: Brussels lace ? Not far off

parts.note: the lace in question is not from Brussels but from a Belgian town a short way from it

explanation.surface: Asked whether some lace comes from Brussels, someone replies that it nearly does.
explanation.walkthrough: Mechlin is the English name of Mechelen, a town about twenty kilometres from Brussels, famous for its bobbin lace.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine bobbin lace named after the Flemish town of Mechelen, close to the Belgian capital.

clue.text: Bridge murderer

definitions.meaning: a form of the card game played by three players, each for themselves
a killer who slashes the victim's neck

explanation.surface: A killer at the card table.
explanation.definitionFit: A variety of three-handed bridge, and a killer who slits throats.

clue.text: Subtil old music-maker

definitions.meaning: Genesis says this creature was more subtil than any beast of the field, so the word stands for the tempter in Eden
an obsolete bass wind instrument of snaking shape

explanation.surface: A crafty musician of olden days.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bible's crafty tempter, and a curved bass wind instrument of the Renaissance and baroque bands.

clue.text: Cecil and Edward are said to be at anchor here

indicators.note: are said means the names are spoken and the sound is what counts

parts.note: Cecil Rhodes was the British colonialist, and Ted is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Two men named Cecil and Edward are reported to be moored here.
explanation.walkthrough: Cecil Rhodes plus Ted (Edward) sounds like the word for a sheltered anchorage.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch of sheltered water outside a harbour where ships can lie at anchor.

clue.text: 28 making silken threads ? .

definitions.meaning: the answer to 28 across, a gambler at dice, who throws them
a worker who twists raw silk into thread

explanation.surface: A gambler who spins silk thread.
explanation.walkthrough: A thrower of dice is a gambler; a silk throwster twists raw silk into yarn.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a dice player, and a worker who twists silk filaments into yarn.

clue.text: "Yorkers prohibited " do they say ?

parts.note: a sign saying no means something is prohibited
a tice is an old cricket term for a yorker, a ball pitched right at the batsman's feet

explanation.surface: A ban on yorkers in cricket: is that what the signs say?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yorkers' looks like people from York; in cricket, a yorker is a ball bowled to land at the batsman's feet, once called a tice. The signs say 'No tices'.
explanation.definitionFit: Posted signs are there to tell people things, so they are what says it.

clue.text: What King Henry's tigers do to their sinews

definitions.text: What King Henry's tigers do to their sinews

parts.words: What King Henry's tigers do to their sinews
parts.note: a reference to the speech in Shakespeare's Henry V urging soldiers to imitate the action of the tiger

explanation.surface: A question about Shakespeare's warlike king and his soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: In Henry V the king cries 'imitate the action of the tiger; stiffen the sinews, summon up the blood'. The OCR added an apostrophe before to.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry V urges his troops, like tigers, to tense and harden their muscles.

clue.text: But he OK's rather than designs your building

definitions.text: But he OK's rather than designs your building

parts.words: But he OK's rather than designs your building
parts.note: the reading turns on a council official whose job is to approve proposed buildings, unlike the architect who draws them

explanation.surface: Someone whose role is to approve a building, not to design it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an architect, the usual planner of buildings, but in Britain the planning officer is the council official who approves or refuses them. The OCR merged he and OK's.
explanation.definitionFit: A council planning officer grants or withholds permission for new building work.

clue.text: Introduce impartial sportsman and step outside

indicators.note: outside means the step's word goes around the official's

parts.note: a pace is a single step
a ref, the referee, is the neutral official in a game

explanation.surface: A fair-minded sportsman is introduced and then asked to step outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; 'outside' puts the step around the referee. 'step outside' reads as an invitation to fight, which hides the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To preface something is to open it with introductory remarks.

clue.text: Apple-winner Herbert tried nothing funny

parts.note: A. P. Herbert was a well-known English humorist and MP, so his initials stand for Herbert

indicators.note: funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters are put in a strange new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Herbert made an attempt that came to nothing, ridiculously.
explanation.walkthrough: Shuffle APH (A. P. Herbert's initials), TRIED and O. In Greek myth Paris gave the golden apple to the fairest goddess.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris awarded the golden apple to the goddess of love over Hera and Athena.

clue.text: Oil is essential to make a tart

indicators.note: to make another word from these letters, they must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Some oil is a necessary ingredient in a tart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is essential' hints that this is an essential oil; 'to make' rearranges A TART.
explanation.definitionFit: Attar is the fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Crazy old king consuming one sort of fatty acid

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so one word swallows the other
crazy means the letters are deranged into a new order

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A mad old king gulps down some fatty acid.
explanation.walkthrough: COLE eats I to make COLIE, and 'Crazy' rearranges that. The OCR garbled the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Oleic acid is the main fatty acid in olive oil.

clue.text: The sort of horse one would be mad to have loose

definitions.text: The sort of horse one would be mad to have loose

parts.words: The sort of horse one would be mad to have loose
parts.note: an old worn-out nag has a slang name that also fits the idiom for a person with something loose in the head

explanation.surface: A horse so wild that letting it run free would be madness.
explanation.walkthrough: A screw is slang for a broken-down horse, and someone with 'a screw loose' is mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a worn-out horse, and the thing a mad person is said to have loose.

clue.text: Priest in Roman church is something of a saint

indicators.note: in means the priest is placed inside the church's letters

parts.note: RC stands for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised the boy Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest in a Catholic church holds something belonging to a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: Eli is the stock crossword priest, from the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: A bone or belonging of a saint kept and venerated after death.

clue.text: Jock has to endure this pin

definitions.meaning: Jock is a Scot, and in Scots and northern dialect this word means to endure or bear
a peg in a boat's gunwale against which an oar pivots

explanation.surface: A Scotsman must put up with this peg.
explanation.walkthrough: Jock is a stock name for a Scotsman, signalling a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots verb meaning bear or suffer, and the peg in a rowing boat's side that holds an oar.

clue.text: Musical bean

definitions.meaning: a small high-pitched wind instrument, so a musical thing
a small pale green variety of kidney bean

explanation.surface: A bean with a talent for music.
explanation.definitionFit: A small end-blown flute, and a small light green haricot bean.

clue.text: Holding one's tongue nice and erect perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the words are one possible arrangement of other letters

explanation.surface: Keeping quiet is pleasant and keeps one upright, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is the anagram signal: rearrange NICE and ERECT together. The OCR put a hyphen in one's tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Reserve or restraint in speech means keeping silent.

clue.text: A game fellow, Hamlet's proverbial perjurer

definitions.meaning: someone who plays at dice, a gambling game
Hamlet speaks of vows as false as these gamblers' oaths

explanation.surface: A sporting chap, the liar Hamlet proverbially mentions.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR cut the clue short; the page adds 'proverbial perjurer'. In Hamlet the prince says marriage vows are made 'as false as dicers' oaths'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dice player is a gamester, and Shakespeare uses the gambler's oath as a byword for a lie.
